description: Canonical HPKE (RFC 9180) suite vocabulary for v1 application-layer public-key sealing surfaces that are NOT carried inside MLS: key-backup `recovery_public_key` envelopes, did_recovery envelopes, to-device sealed material (`ck.secret.send`), member-application reviewer envelopes and file-transfer key envelopes. An HPKE suite names the (KEM, KDF, AEAD) triple; its canonical_id is the wire scheme / `hpke_suite` selector value. The KEM (DHKEM-X25519-HKDF-SHA256) and KDF (HKDF-SHA256) use RFC 9180 primitive ids, but the application-layer seal/open transcript is a Cokret-specific base-mode DH-box (ephemeral X25519 -> X25519-DH with the recipient key -> HKDF-SHA256 over a caller-supplied info transcript binding the ephemeral and recipient public keys -> AEAD), NOT RFC 9180's SetupBaseS / key_schedule / LabeledExtract / LabeledExpand with an internally derived base_nonce. This is the fourth algorithm-agility registry, symmetric to signature-alg-registry.json, digest-suite-registry.json and mls-ciphersuite-registry.json. MLS group messages keep their own HPKE internals via mls-ciphersuite-registry.json and are out of scope here.
suite_id_grammar: suite_id = 'ck.hpke_' kem_id '_aead_' aead_id '.v' major ; each id segment matches [a-z0-9]+ . The canonical_id is the full wire string; it is NOT freely composed from parts — only suites present as rows below exist, and only status=active rows are valid on wire.
registry_rules: Only suites present as rows in this registry exist. Implementations MUST NOT compose KEM/KDF/AEAD ids freely; only status=active rows are valid on wire.

A suite id not present as an active row MUST fail closed with unsupported_hpke_suite when it appears in an HPKE-sealed surface (key-backup recipient_method=recovery_public_key, ck.secret.send, member-application encryption_envelope, file-transfer key_envelope). Receivers MUST NOT infer suite parameters from the AEAD name alone.

Schema enum values for HPKE suite selector fields (e.g. ck.schema.key_backup.v1 encryption.hpke_suite, the ck.secret.send / member-application / file-transfer envelope `scheme` const) MUST be generated from active rows' canonical_id.

When a surface carries both an explicit `hpke_suite` selector and an AEAD `name`/profile field, the AEAD MUST equal the selected suite's aead; a mismatch MUST be rejected (schema_violation). A surface MAY omit the selector only where a single default-MUST suite is pinned by its defining document, in which case the absent selector denotes that row.

status=reserved rows pin the wire id and profile gate but MUST NOT appear on wire until every activation_requirements entry is met and the row is flipped to active in a registry release. Receivers MUST fail closed (unsupported_hpke_suite) on a reserved suite id seen on wire before activation.

The registry is intentionally minimal: new KEM families (post-quantum / hybrid), new KDFs and new AEADs enter additively as new rows with their own profile gates and conformance vectors; the ck.hpke_*_aead_*.v* wire form needs no rewrite. Nonce handling is per-surface, not RFC 9180 key-schedule-derived: the `recovery_public_key` / did_recovery envelopes carry a fresh random 24-byte XChaCha nonce on the wire (`enc` plus nonce||ciphertext), while the single-use to-device `ck.secret.send` seal uses a fixed zero nonce that is safe only because every seal mints a fresh ephemeral key. Implementations MUST preserve each surface's nonce discipline; see zh/identity/key-management.md §7.5 for the symmetric key-backup nonce-uniqueness rules.

kem_strength_order.note: Classical KEMs are treated as equal classical strength; the hybrid xwing row is strictly stronger (adds ML-KEM-768 post-quantum confidentiality). Consumed by any future no-downgrade rule on suite transition.

suites.security_note: v1 default-MUST application-layer HPKE suite. KEM DHKEM(X25519, HKDF-SHA256) and KDF HKDF-SHA256 are RFC 9180 base; the AEAD is XChaCha20-Poly1305 (extended 192-bit nonce, outside RFC 9180's base AEAD registry but widely implemented), retained as the v1 default for the to-device / member-application / file-transfer envelopes that already pin this id. Classical (not post-quantum).
All-RFC-9180 suite for key-backup recovery_public_key envelopes on platforms with AES hardware acceleration. Classical.
All-RFC-9180 suite (96-bit-nonce ChaCha20-Poly1305) for software-only platforms preferring the base RFC 9180 AEAD over the extended-nonce XChaCha variant. Classical.
P-256 KEM for WebAuthn/FIDO2/PKI key-agreement interop, mirroring the ECDSA-P256 signature row. Profile-gated; receivers not advertising ck.profile.hpke.p256.v1 fail closed. Classical.

activation_requirements: ck.profile.kem.hybrid_xwing.v1 fully specified with the X-Wing KEM draft pinned (draft-connolly-cfrg-xwing-kem) under MIMI-style draft-pinning discipline (draft change = new profile version)
Per-suite HPKE conformance vectors published (KEM encap/decap, key schedule, sealed bytes)

Coverage-priority alignment recorded: key-backup envelope before MLS KeyPackage (static ciphertext backups are the primary Harvest-Now-Decrypt-Later target; reuses the reserved ck.aead.hybrid_kem.* namespace)
suites.security_note: Reserved post-quantum hybrid KEM (X25519 + ML-KEM-768) per the encryption-and-audit.md §2 PQ roadmap. Hybrid confidentiality: secure if either X25519 or ML-KEM-768 holds. Not on wire until activated.
